system_description.narrative_title: A precarious multipolar order: tech shocks, energy wars, and market stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is being reshaped by simultaneous, interacting shocks: an AI-driven industrial transformation that is straining labour markets, corporate strategy and financial stability; renewed kinetic and gray‑zone conflicts (notably the US–Iran exchanges and Russia’s campaign in Ukraine) that are amplifying energy and security insecurities; and heavy monetary‑fiscal stress as central bankers pivot and long-term bond yields surge. These processes are tightly coupled — energy shocks feed inflation and market volatility, which in turn constrain policy choices as states weaponize assets and resources (oil, sanctions, investment) to project power and defend interests. The result is an open, fast‑moving system in which technological displacement, geopolitics, and financial forces continually reconfigure alliances, trade, and risk perceptions.
system_description.scope: The global political‑economic‑security system in 2026: major states and alliances (US, China, Russia, EU, NATO members, Middle Eastern powers), transnational corporations and tech ecosystems (AI, semiconductors, robotics), global energy and commodity flows, international finance and central banks, sanctions and trade regimes, and ongoing conflict theatres and regional security complexes.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑technical and ecological system — the broader human system embedding politics, economics, technology, and the Earth’s resource base.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system and capital markets (sovereign debt, bond markets, central banks)
Energy and commodity system (oil, gas, helium, strategic minerals, supply chains)
Advanced technology and AI‑industrial complex (AI models, chips, robotics, software ecosystems)
Regional security complexes (Middle East conflict dynamics; Europe–Russia security; Indo‑Pacific tensions)

variables.name: U.S.–Iran military escalation
variables.description: Direct and proxy combat between the United States and Iran is intensifying, shifting regional military postures, prompting reciprocal strikes and sanctions, and raising risks to maritime security and wider Middle East stability.

variables.name: Russia’s war in Ukraine and European gray‑zone attacks
variables.description: Russia's sustained invasion of Ukraine and an accompanying campaign of strikes and 'gray zone' operations across Europe are reshaping battlefield control, European defence postures and NATO deterrence calculations.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology and economic rivalry
variables.description: An escalating strategic competition between the United States and China over semiconductors, AI, investment screening and trade policy is realigning industrial supply chains, export controls and global tech governance.

variables.name: U.S. reallocation of Venezuelan energy assets
variables.description: U.S. moves to assume operational stakes and long‑term control of Venezuelan oil reserves are reallocating hydrocarbon resources, altering energy market leverage and creating new geopolitical leverage points in the Americas.

variables.name: Global monetary and bond‑market stress
variables.description: A surge in long‑term yields, hawkish central‑bank rhetoric and rising policy friction between monetary and fiscal authorities are shifting the global debt landscape and heightening systemic financial‑stability and capital‑flow risks.
